original.target_description: Experiment 1 item-level correlations between misinformation availability (standard-condition recognition endorsement proxy) and change in the misinformation effect with double versus standard misinformation, operationalised as misinformation endorsement. Both recognition and cued recall tests are reported; the supplied locator does not identify which test.

n.sample_role: Critical items in Experiment 1; item-level correlation observations, not the 42 participants. Three listed items featured in all experiments; fourth item added in Experiment 2.
n.exclusions: Author manuscript p. 12 states: There were no outliers that needed to be removed for data analysis; all relevant data points were used.

replication.target_description: Single replication study, item-level correlation between misinformation availability and double-minus-standard misinformation-effect change, operationalised as misinformation endorsement; eight critical items separately in high and low availability conditions.

n.quote: resulting in 16 data points underlying the reported correlations.
n.sample_role: Item-by-misinformation-availability-condition data points (eight items in each of two conditions); not participants.
n.exclusions: No item-level exclusions stated; footnote 9 explicitly includes each of the eight critical items in both conditions.

reported_success.location: Author manuscript p. 27, MA and the misinformation effect – correlational evidence
reported_success.quote: We partly replicated an item analysis first performed in Blank et al. (2022)

notes: Original study identifier 1 was respected as Experiment 1. Its recognition and cued-recall correlations differ, and the empty locator does not select a test; therefore original es is null rather than arbitrarily choosing one. Original p is not reported separately for those Experiment 1 tests. Aggregate correlations across Experiments 1–3 and their p values were not substituted. Original n=3 identifies the item-level analysis unit. Replication p and r refer to the same item-level test. Authors give a partial-replication narrative for the item analysis overall; mixed records that narrative rather than inferring an outcome-specific success label from significance.
